items.instructions: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word on the left.

items.prompt: employ

explanation.en: To employ someone and to hire someone both mean to give them a job.

items.prompt: resign

explanation.en: To resign is the formal way to say to quit a job.

items.prompt: wage

explanation.en: Both are money paid for work. A wage is often paid weekly and a salary monthly, but they are close in meaning.

items.prompt: co-worker

explanation.en: A co-worker is a colleague: someone you work with.

items.prompt: delay

explanation.en: To delay a meeting is to postpone it: to move it to a later time.

items.instructions: Choose the word that matches each definition.

items.prompt: the amount of work someone has to do

explanation.en: Workload is the amount of work a person has.

items.prompt: the date by which a piece of work must be finished

explanation.en: A deadline is the latest time to finish something.

items.prompt: time worked beyond your normal hours

explanation.en: Overtime is the extra time you work, or the money paid for it.

items.prompt: a move to a more important job in the same organisation

explanation.en: A promotion moves you to a higher position.

items.prompt: to travel regularly between home and work

explanation.en: To commute is to make the regular journey to and from work.

items.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best word.

items.prompt: After the merger, forty members of staff were made ___.

explanation.en: Be made redundant means to lose your job because it is no longer needed.

items.prompt: We need to ___ two more engineers before the project starts.

explanation.en: To recruit is to find and employ new people.

items.prompt: As a ___ translator, she chooses which projects to accept.

explanation.en: Freelance workers are not employed by one company, so they choose their projects.

items.prompt: Hospital porters often have to work a night ___.

explanation.en: A night shift is a period of work at night.

items.prompt: He decided to ___ after twenty years with the firm.

explanation.en: To resign is to leave your job by your own decision.

items.instructions: Choose the word that is most often used with the words on the left.

items.prompt: get a …

explanation.en: Get a promotion is a very common collocation.

items.prompt: do …

explanation.en: We say do overtime, with no article.

items.prompt: a heavy …

explanation.en: A heavy workload means a lot of work.

items.prompt: a tight …

explanation.en: A tight deadline leaves very little time.

items.prompt: earn a …

explanation.en: Earn a living means to earn enough money to live on.

items.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best word.

items.prompt: She has had a very successful ___ in advertising.

explanation.en: A career is your working life in one field. Careful: a university course is a degree.
explanation.es: Career es la trayectoria profesional, no la carrera universitaria.

items.prompt: I'm going to ___ for the manager's job.

explanation.en: You apply for a job.

items.prompt: I usually have lunch with my ___ from the office.

explanation.en: Colleagues are the people you work with.

items.prompt: Can I take a day ___ next Friday?

explanation.en: Take a day off means not to work on a working day.

items.prompt: It takes me an hour to ___ to work every morning.

explanation.en: To commute is to travel between home and work.
